**Finding submitted: MISSING (medium severity)**

**What I found.** Article XXI "Effect of Termination" (p0138) is entirely one-directional: on termination our licenses end, we must ship all Licensed Technology, API documentation and Confidential Information back to Licensor within five days and certify compliance, and "All of the Licensor's rights under this Agreement shall survive termination."

**What is absent.** Nothing anywhere in the agreement obliges Licensor to help us exit or to give our data back:
- Searches for data return, export and transition returned no results.
- The confidentiality article (p0124–p0125) imposes duties only on Licensee; there is no counterpart return obligation on Licensor.
- No wind-down heading exists in Articles XIX–XXIII or the General Provisions.

This matters because the platform is hosted — we use it to receive market data and enter trading tickets (p0033), so our trade and order records live in Licensor's systems. As drafted we would exit with no export right, which sits at or below the playbook walk-away line ("no data return").

**Redline (validated ok:true).** New Article XXI(c) inserted after p0138 requiring Licensor to: (i) provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at then-current rates on our request; (ii) return all Licensee Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format within thirty days; and (iii) thereafter delete it and certify deletion in writing. I included a short definition of "Licensee Data" inline because the agreement has no such defined term. The comment offers the fallback of ninety days' assistance, provided the thirty-day export right is preserved.
